title: Mobile Product Claim v1
description: WBS-50.05 Mobile product claims. The roadmap's own words: 'Journey Passport may reference claims like: completion; crash-free rate; latency; return usage. Mobile technical PASS never silently resolves product-success claims.' claim-lifecycle-v1 (WBS-50.01) is explicit that a claim's own asserted content is deferred to later WBS-50 units; this is that content for the mobile-product domain, mirroring claim-mdm-quality-v1's own floor/tolerance shape (WBS-50.04) rather than claim-score-v1's probabilistic-forecast shape. Joined to a claim-lifecycle-v1 record by claim_id + revision_id, the same join shape claim-evidence-v1, claim-score-v1 and claim-mdm-quality-v1 already use (scripts/mobile_product_claims.py's check_matches_lifecycle), and to a journey_passport.py composed passport via journey_id plus that passport's own production.record.claim_ids array -- journey_passport.py's own documented hook point for 'a production-claims module' that is 'not listed at all yet' (its own module docstring), never a second hook invented here. The critical structural rule this schema and its binding module exist to enforce: journey_passport.py's technical dimensions (contract, build_identity, functional, accessibility, performance, visual, physical_device, release) measure whether the reference mobile build installs, launches, and runs correctly -- never whether real production users actually complete this journey, stay crash-free, see acceptable latency, or return. A mobile product claim therefore never resolves from a technical PASS; it resolves only from real product/analytics evidence, which this codebase does not yet have a source for (see scripts/mobile_product_claims.py's NO_EVIDENCE_REASONS), so measured_value/resolved_at stay null (honest NO-DATA) until a real evidence source exists. Only the keyword subset the sibling WBS-50 schemas already enforce is used here: type, required, properties, enum, const, additionalProperties.

schema_version.description: Which shape this record follows, so a reader never has to guess.

claim_id.description: Must match the claim-lifecycle-v1 record's claim_id for the same claim (checked by check_matches_lifecycle) and must appear in the journey_passport's own production.record.claim_ids array (checked by check_matches_passport).

revision_id.description: Must match the claim-lifecycle-v1 record's revision_id: scoring resolves one exact historical revision, never a rewritten successor (WBS-50.01's own scoring-target rule, reused here rather than re-argued).

journey_id.description: The journey_passport.py composed passport's own 'journey' field (itself mobile_journey_contract.py's journey_id, read through) this claim was registered for.

product_dimension.description: One of the four example product claims the roadmap names for WBS-50.05 (completion, crash-free rate, latency, return usage). Named as examples in the roadmap's own words, not stated as an exhaustive closed list in principle, but this schema version enumerates exactly those four; a project needing a fifth extends the enum in a later schema version rather than smuggling a new value past additionalProperties:false.

comparison.description: Which direction real operational evidence must respect the threshold: gte for a floor (measured_value must be at or above threshold, e.g. completion, crash_free_rate, return_usage), lte for a ceiling (measured_value must be at or below threshold, e.g. latency).

threshold.description: The floor or ceiling value itself. Frozen before this claim is relied on (scripts/claim_lifecycle.py's FROZEN state semantics, reused not reinvented): once the matching claim-lifecycle-v1 revision reaches FROZEN, this value may not change without a correction (a new revision_id).

measured_value.description: The real product/analytics evidence value once resolved, or null while unresolved. Must be null exactly when resolved_at is null, and non-null exactly when resolved_at is non-null (checked by hand: the enforced keyword subset has no if/then). Never set from journey_passport.py's technical field_verdicts -- a technical PASS is not product evidence and must never resolve this field.

resolved_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp real product/analytics evidence resolved this claim, or null while unresolved.

evidence_note.description: A short, human-readable note naming what real evidence resolved this claim (or, honestly, why none exists yet to resolve it, and which journey_passport technical dimensions were deliberately not used to resolve it). May be set even while measured_value/resolved_at stay null, to record the reason for an honest NO-DATA rather than leaving it unexplained.
